posts.title: An agent benchmark needs a resource budget

claims.claim: Terminal-Bench 2.0 infrastructure errors at 1×, 3×, and uncapped were 5.8%, 2.1%, and 0.5%. Task success rose six points from strict to uncapped.
claims.limit: Anthropic's controlled resource sweep; the magnitude does not generalize across all agent evals.

claims.claim: Strict to 3× lowered infra errors by 3.7 percentage points.

posts.title: A canary needs enough traffic to fail

claims.claim: 5% of traffic failing 20% of the time gives a 1% fleet error rate.
claims.basis: Google SRE workbook example; clean control and proportional traffic exposure.

claims.claim: Cloudflare's main impact was mitigated at 14:30 UTC; all operations were restored at 17:06 UTC.
claims.limit: Two separate milestones in the company incident timeline.

claims.claim: One-in-10,000 and one-in-1,000 failure probabilities need 29,956 and 2,995 requests for 95% detection.
claims.limit: IID canary traffic and perfect event detection; correlation, cohort skew and noisy metrics can change sample requirements.

posts.title: An online migration can quietly lose its rollback

claims.claim: Stripe's source system had hundreds of millions of subscription objects and used a staged migration.
claims.limit: Order and scale of the reported migration, without assuming downtime or throughput.

claims.claim: GitHub's May 4 incident reported about 1.3% peak and 0.46% average 5xx requests.
claims.limit: Customer request error rates during the incident; the report does not identify the specific migration tool.

claims.claim: At read cutover both stores hold revision 2; after a new-only write a restored old reader still sees 2.
claims.limit: Assumes no reverse replication or replay before rollback.
